title: Read-only code context MCP
summary: Add a read-only local MCP adapter over the existing token-bounded repository context catalog, configure Codex and Claude Code, and reduce ordinary AI navigation token use.
reason: AI clients can use the generated context catalog only through a fresh CLI process or broad filesystem discovery. A long-lived, bounded MCP surface can reuse the catalog, search current code, and return small source ranges without loading broad indexes or duplicated startup documentation.
behavior_before: Codex and Claude have no repository-specific MCP server. Agents must invoke the context_slice CLI or perform repeated filesystem discovery, and Claude's local instructions duplicate older broad startup guidance.
behavior_after: Codex and Claude share a local read-only stdio MCP server with four bounded tools for task context, catalog lookup, live code search, and ranged code reads. One MCP-first startup workflow has a context_slice fallback and measurable token ceilings.

Measured warm repo_context median 9.02 ms and live code_search median 97.63 ms over the 2,410-record working index
Codex mcp get and Claude mcp get (Codex enabled; Claude connected; both point to the isolated LocalBase environment)
Token review: combined AGENTS/Claude/schema/default-context estimate 7,427 tokens; conservative schema ceiling 7,869; legacy baseline 9,967
rollback_plan: Remove the mediapipeline-code registrations from Codex and Claude, remove the isolated LocalBase/Tooling/code-context-mcp environment, then revert only this packet's service, MCP adapter, setup script, dependency, tests, documentation, inventory, and generated-summary changes. Do not alter the predecessor packet or unrelated dirty files.
notes: The predecessor context-navigation packet remains in progress but its focused ContextRecord/context_slice/feature-card tests pass.
